purpose: A proposed production path toward AAA-quality finish, not a claim of current AAA status, a funded schedule or platform certification.
policy: Canonical delivery statuses change only in a reviewed source commit. Browser checkmarks are local review notes, not proof of implementation. Proposed targets require owner approval. Preserve all six chapters, saves, sibling applications and asset credits.

statusDefinitions.Planned: Not implemented to the stated criterion.
statusDefinitions.Implemented: A working foundation exists; the full criterion still needs review.
statusDefinitions.Automated: The specifically scoped automated criterion has evidence; physical devices and player enjoyment are not certified.
statusDefinitions.Blocked: The approval gate depends on unfinished work.
statusDefinitions.Approved: The criterion has a named reviewer and recorded sign-off.

phases.name: Release foundation
phases.goal: Close regressions before adding more content.
phases.gate: All supported input paths start, save, reload and produce audio without uncaught errors.

phases.name: Flagship vertical slice
phases.goal: Make one complete segment worth playing repeatedly.
phases.gate: A 15-20 minute Floodgate slice passes an art review and a recorded, independent player test.

phases.name: Combat and stealth
phases.goal: Make each encounter readable, fair and expressive.
phases.gate: Melee, ranged, evasion, detection and resource economies hold up across repeat encounters.

phases.name: Campaign and world
phases.goal: Expand authored variety rather than duplicating rooms.
phases.gate: Every chapter has a distinct route, pacing plan, task arc and verified beginning-to-end playthrough.

phases.name: Art and animation
phases.goal: Bring characters and places to a consistent production standard.
phases.gate: Camera-matched art reviews approve the hero, enemies, animation, architecture, effects and lighting.

phases.name: Sound and music
phases.goal: Make sound useful, emotional and dependable.
phases.gate: Every audible action has an appropriate cue; music transitions and mixes pass measured and listening reviews.

phases.name: Accessibility and performance
phases.goal: Measure the actual target devices and input methods.
phases.gate: The agreed hardware matrix meets its frame-time, memory, readability and accessibility targets.

phases.name: Release and production
phases.goal: Ship a supported game with repeatable evidence.
phases.gate: Release blockers are closed, rights are documented, saves migrate, and a rollback has been rehearsed.

items.title: Audio context rate compatibility
items.acceptance: Audio graph renders at 24, 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz; live playback starts after a permitted user action.

items.title: Independent chapter shelter saves
items.acceptance: Six chapter checkpoints coexist; restarting one changes no other slot; current legacy saves migrate without loss.

items.title: Controller-reachable equipment
items.acceptance: Select each gun and tool in the satchel, then return using B; keyboard and touch have the same equipment access.

items.title: Finite inventory and save validation
items.acceptance: Reloading, switching, pickup, restore and cancellation cannot duplicate ammunition, supplies or completed tasks.

items.title: Current native acceptance suite
items.acceptance: All native journeys run on the exact release source; failures remain visible and no required assertions are skipped.

items.title: Controller and audio device acceptance
items.acceptance: Record wired and Bluetooth Xbox playthroughs with menus, disconnect, audio activation, crafting and healing on real hardware.

items.title: Save recovery and write-failure handling
items.acceptance: Corrupt primary data recovers a valid backup; storage failure never overwrites the last valid primary or legacy mirror.

items.title: Versioned production checklist
items.acceptance: Each task has an owner role, priority, acceptance criterion, status, dependencies and evidence; every release updates the board.

items.title: Vertical-slice design lock
items.acceptance: Approve one 15-20 minute Floodgate slice: approach, stealth, discovery, escalation, recovery and extraction, with no filler.

items.title: Readable first encounter
items.acceptance: First-time players identify cover, patrol direction and their objective without needing an outside explanation.

items.title: Playable alternate approach
items.acceptance: The slice supports at least two meaningfully different routes; both are collision-tested and have different risk/reward.

items.title: Stealth-to-combat-to-recovery pacing
items.acceptance: A recorded playthrough moves through all three states without unavoidable damage, empty downtime or an inventory dead end.

items.title: Environmental story beat
items.acceptance: An original scene communicates who lived here and why the player should care, using space and interaction rather than a text dump.

items.title: Hero scene art benchmark
items.acceptance: Approve fixed-camera images and motion captures of the slice in daylight, rain and interior lighting.

items.title: Independent player study
items.acceptance: Record five unfamiliar players; proposed gate: at least four complete the slice and explain core controls without intervention.

items.title: Slice approval gate
items.acceptance: Game owner approves the complete slice after playtest, art review and hardware/performance review; record rejected points too.

items.title: Survival controller action mapping
items.acceptance: Tap/hold B, X melee, LB dodge, RB listen, LT+X reload and menu controls remain distinct and neutral-arm after mode changes.

items.title: Telegraphed enemy attack windows
items.acceptance: Windup, impact, recovery and counter windows are visually and audibly legible for every enemy role.

items.title: Melee hit reaction and tools
items.acceptance: Contacts respect range, facing, walls, stamina and durability; animation and feedback must be reviewed at game speed.

items.title: Ranged weapon handling polish
items.acceptance: Tune aim speed, recoil, spread, reticle and reload poses on controller; validate sidearm and rifle as distinct choices.

items.title: Patrol communication and search variety
items.acceptance: Enemies share only plausible information, search a remembered location, flank through navigable routes and eventually stand down.

items.title: Human-shield grab prototype
items.acceptance: Prototype the requested grab with animation, escape/release, enemy response, controller prompts and non-blocking state transitions.

items.title: Deployable distraction/trap tool
items.acceptance: Add a finite, craftable deployable with clear placement preview, enemy interaction, counters, cleanup and checkpoint rules.

items.title: Resource economy playtest
items.acceptance: Record stealth, mixed and combat-heavy runs; demonstrate recovery paths without infinite resource farming or mandatory grinding.

items.title: Six authored expedition foundations
items.acceptance: Floodgate, Conservatory, Terminus, Meridian, Breakwater and Whiteout retain distinct footprints, objectives and physical puzzle gates.

items.title: Chapter task and dependency graph
items.acceptance: Required work blocks extraction correctly; optional work remains optional; rewards and journal state survive checkpoints.

items.title: Campaign progression and chapter saves
items.acceptance: Continue the chosen chapter or latest shelter without erasing other expeditions; distinguish unsaved progress clearly.

items.title: Chapter route and pacing audit
items.acceptance: Review all six chapters for landmarks, shortcuts, sightlines, supply spacing, backtracking and encounter rhythm.

items.title: New puzzle interaction families
items.acceptance: Build a prototype unlike the existing wheels or linked breakers, with in-world clues, reset safety and optional layered hints.

items.title: Collision-authored window and ledge traversal
items.acceptance: Build supported windows, ledges and gaps with valid starts/landings, camera clearance and enemy navigation; do not promise arbitrary traversal.

items.title: Swimming and water encounter design
items.acceptance: Prototype buoyancy, boundaries, exit points, camera, input and enemy interactions together before introducing swim-required routes.

items.title: Complete campaign playthrough evidence
items.acceptance: Record each chapter from start through all required work to extraction with ordinary inputs, preserving exact build and save evidence.

items.title: Original visual direction bible
items.acceptance: Approve proportions, silhouettes, architecture, materials, palette and visual hierarchy; use references for direction, not copied assets.

items.title: Production hero character
items.acceptance: Build an original coherent hero mesh with clothing layers, facial detail, UVs and LODs; compare against the current procedural rig.

items.title: Authored locomotion and action clips
items.acceptance: Approve walk, run, crouch, crawl, turn, aim, reload, strike, stagger, vault, heal and craft transitions without visible snapping.

items.title: Foot placement and hand contacts
items.acceptance: Feet follow slopes and stairs; hands align to weapons and traversal contacts; solve IK failures without destabilizing gameplay.

items.title: Enemy silhouettes and reactions
items.acceptance: Every enemy role is recognizable in silhouette and motion, with distinct clothing/body treatment and readable damage states.

items.title: Architecture and prop production kit
items.acceptance: Replace conspicuous repeated blocks with an original modular kit, trim details, usable interiors and authored wear at consistent scale.

items.title: Lighting and VFX scene continuity
items.acceptance: Review interior/exterior transitions, shadows, rain, puddles, smoke, muzzle flashes and restrained effects on both graphics tiers.

items.title: Asset optimization and provenance
items.acceptance: Every imported asset retains source/license/hash records; final hero and environment assets also need LOD, memory and streaming review.

items.title: Original six-chapter adaptive score
items.acceptance: Six distinct arrangements respond to danger and listening; composition quality and emotional pacing still require listening review.

items.title: Stereo direction and obstacle muffling
items.acceptance: Source distance and camera orientation affect output; walls muffle sounds; mono does not remove caption direction.

items.title: Layered Foley and action cues
items.acceptance: Movement surfaces, shots, reload stages, impacts, cloth, crafting, healing, creatures, mechanisms and supplies have distinct cues.

items.title: Authored Foley listening pass
items.acceptance: Review loudness, texture, timing, repetition and material realism for every cue on headphones and speakers; replace weak placeholders.

items.title: Room-aware reverb and sound portals
items.acceptance: Interiors, streets, tunnels and courtyards use coherent acoustic transitions without leaking high-cost node allocation.

items.title: Musical transitions and dramatic silence
items.acceptance: Author bar-aligned transitions, exploration variation, combat exit and silence so the score does not loop mechanically or mask cues.

items.title: Mixer accessibility and output budgets
items.acceptance: Independent sliders, mono, night mix and captions remain controller reachable; voice and sample-cache budgets stay bounded.

items.title: Final mix and device listening approval
items.acceptance: Measure peaks and dynamic range, then record subjective approval on headphones, laptop speakers and a TV with real controller play.

items.title: Full remapping and hold alternatives
items.acceptance: Offer remapping, conflict resolution, hold/toggle alternatives and readable per-device prompts; test every resulting action path.

items.title: Caption and interface readability
items.acceptance: Review text size, contrast, safe areas, caption direction, speaker identification and color-independent signals across target displays.

items.title: Reduced motion and adjustable HUD
items.acceptance: Players can reduce environmental motion and disable quiet-HUD fading without removing necessary gameplay information.

items.title: Target hardware matrix
items.acceptance: Name the actual CPU/GPU/RAM, browser, display resolution, controller and audio device for each supported tier before claiming performance.

items.title: Repeatable performance capture
items.acceptance: Record p50/p95/p99 frame time, long frames, draw calls, memory and load time on a fixed route and exact build.

items.title: Frame-time acceptance
items.acceptance: Proposed targets, not current claims: desktop 1080p/60 fps and reduced tier 30 fps; agree hardware and pass sustained representative scenes.

items.title: Memory, streaming and graphics recovery
items.acceptance: Bound assets and caches, test repeated chapter swaps, slow downloads and WebGL context loss; preserve checkpoint data on recovery.

items.title: Browser and device regression matrix
items.acceptance: Run agreed browser/OS/controller combinations, phones and focus-loss scenarios; scope VR separately from desktop certification.

items.title: Staffing, budget and ownership plan
items.acceptance: Assign real owners and review capacity; estimate content and asset costs before setting a release date. Roles here are not staffing claims.

items.title: Deterministic builds and evidence
items.acceptance: Link every release to exact source, test reports, asset manifest and published file hashes; keep failed evidence.

items.title: Asset rights and public-source boundary
items.acceptance: Check licensed assets, vendored notices, local runtime imports and absence of confidential material or service credentials.

items.title: Long-session and save migration QA
items.acceptance: Run proposed two-hour sessions with repeated deaths, restarts, chapter changes and old saves; log every regression and reproduction.

items.title: Player-facing known issues and support
items.acceptance: Publish supported devices, known limitations, save recovery instructions and a clear issue-reporting path before release.

items.title: Rollback rehearsal
items.acceptance: Rehearse reverting a release without deleting saves or changing sibling games, then verify public hashes again.

items.title: Optional platform expansion decision
items.acceptance: Decide separately whether full VR, native packaging or multiplayer serves the game; each needs its own cost, input and QA plan.

items.title: Release candidate approval
items.acceptance: Close critical defects and obtain player, art, audio, accessibility and hardware sign-off. A green checklist alone is not AAA quality.
